findings.note: Every passing check in the contract rests on a byte-identity claim the bundle falsifies. The contract states 'the live staged ... resolve-project-context.py is byte-identical (sha256 7d59debc63422f9ea20ab4042343d3284dade87f6bb0aad69ee77c7214da19ed) to the report's own Outputs-table claim, so the recorded green-sh.log/green-ps1.log ... describe the exact code this contract also just re-ran'; the bundle marks that path (and MANIFEST.sha256, CHANGELOG.md, and tests/resolve-project-context-block-check.py) STALE against the report. The bundled driver's main() runs TEN T-003 cases plus FOUR run_t004_case cases, while every recorded log (red 78/24, green 102/0, qg focused-tests 102/0) enumerates only SIX T-003 cases and no T-004 case. The recorded RED/GREEN and re-run evidence therefore does not describe the code under review, and no test result in this bundle can be credited.

Four T-003 fixtures present in the bundled driver -- 'resolve-component-paths-launch-failed', 'registry-discovery-unimportable', 'evaluate-predicate-output-malformed', 'dsl-warn-unsorted-affected-components' -- appear in no log anywhere in the bundle (red-sh/red-ps1/green-sh/green-ps1/focused-tests-sh/focused-tests-ps1 all stop at the original six). The AC-056 per-node `severity: "warn"` diagnostics behaviour implemented in _warn_diagnostic_detail/_evaluate_capabilities is likewise unevidenced: the recorded 'exact Resolver Evidence' assertions were captured before that behaviour existed. These acceptance checks are asserted but unverified.

The bundled implementation is not T-003's increment. Its docstring reads 'implementation stages T-002+T-003+T-004 (steps 0-13)' and main() contains the track branch (10a/10b), Resolver Evidence assembly, step-12 self-validation and step-13 recheck -- all explicitly Out of Scope for T-003 ('never assembles the track-branch output or Resolver Evidence itself (T-004's own scope)', tasks.md T-003 Goal/Out of Scope). T-003's Done-When 'git diff --stat confirms this task's own diff' cannot be evaluated against these bytes, and the steps 4-9 increment cannot be reviewed in isolation from the bundle as assembled.

design.md API/Contract Plan step 9 requires 'A full Resolver Evidence record ... maximally informative for the caller diagnosing it'. By step 9 all five context_binding fields (full_context_revision, projection_sha256, registry_digest, ownership_digest, dependency_pointers) and the resolver block are already computed, yet _write_evidence emits only {schema, feature, capability_evaluations, diagnostics, state} and drops context_binding and resolver entirely. design.md step 1 justifies their absence only because 'no Registry/ownership/projection step ever ran' -- a justification that does not hold at step 9. REQ-004 provenance binding is lost on the one Block path this task owns.

design.md step 6 says 'Invoke generate-registry-digest --whole (Epic A2) against the located Registry', and the Data Plan B8 snapshot rule pins 'the discovered Registry's own bytes'. The implementation invokes ['generate-registry-digest', '--whole'] with no registry argument and relies on the subprocess repeating its own ADR-0025 discovery (its own docstring concedes this). context_binding.registry_digest is therefore never provably bound to the registry_path/registry_document that step 5 validated and steps 7-8 evaluated against; a discovery divergence between the two resolutions would publish a digest for a different Registry with no diagnostic.

When an affected component returned by resolve-component-paths has no entry in the Context Projection, the resolver silently substitutes empty properties and evaluates the trigger/when predicate against fabricated `{}` input, emitting no diagnostic. Data Plan 'Context Projection read set' specifies the payload as 'the whole projectedComponent object' and the feature's governing rule is Block-when-ambiguous. A predicate that returns a clean `no-match` (rather than a `warn`) against empty properties silently under-matches a Capability -- exactly the failure mode T-003's own Risk Rationale names -- with no Block and no record of the substitution. The 'dsl-warn-unsorted-affected-components' fixture bakes this `{}` substitution into its expectations rather than rejecting it.

Registry fields are indexed unguarded on the assumption that validate-capability-registry covers them. A missing key raises an uncaught KeyError, so the process exits with a raw Python traceback on stderr instead of the single canonical `capability-resolver: <id>: <detail>` line (AC-014/M8) and with no Resolver Evidence written at all -- and the traceback embeds absolute filesystem paths, which security-spec.md's no-local-path containment forbids. This is the same class the bundled driver's own 'registry-discovery-unimportable' fixture was added to close for ImportError; no fixture covers the KeyError path.

design.md step 4 requires --source-rev/--target-rev/--include-untracked be passed to resolve-component-paths 'verbatim, byte-for-byte identical to the values this invocation itself received'. The code synthesizes a `--no-include-untracked` flag the Resolver's own CLI never accepted when --include-untracked was omitted. Whether Epic A3 accepts that spelling cannot be checked from the bundle.

design.md describes classification on 'the dependency's own stable canonicalizer-failed: error-class prefix'. The code does an unanchored substring test, `if "canonicalizer-failed" in stderr_text`, so any occurrence of that token anywhere in upstream stderr re-routes a generic non-zero exit to canonicalizer-invocation-failed instead of dependency-subprocess-failed.

The GREEN accounting is contradicted by its own log. The report claims '102 = T-002's own 96 assertions + this task's own 24 new + 2 suite-registration ... net +6 over T-002's own 96'. focused-tests-sh.log decomposes as 72 non-T-003 assertions + 30 T-003 assertions (six fixtures x five, not four) = 102. The pass/fail totals reconcile only because six of the thirty T-003 assertions pass vacuously in RED; the stated baseline of 96 does not exist.

The contract comment still carries 'HONEST FINDING, not smoothed over: task-state-check is recorded below as passes:false/required:true, which will itself make check-contract report this contract FAILED' while the checks array records passes:true, reconciled only by a trailing 'Re-recorded 2026-08-19' sentence -- the narrative and the machine-readable record disagree on their face. Separately, traceability.log cites 'run_t003_case() (line 247)' and 'CASE_NAMES (line 160-165)'; the bundled driver has no CASE_NAMES symbol (it is ALL_CASE_NAMES) and run_t003_case sits several hundred lines later, so the traceability evidence was written against a different file revision.
